summary: Master DHIS2, WHO DQR, and donor reporting frameworks in this 5-day hands-on training. Build dashboards, assess data quality, and report with confidence.
lede: Digital monitoring and reporting helps health programme teams turn routine HMIS data into evidence for decisions and programme reports. This course is for mid-career M&E professionals and health information officers with practical experience using a health information system or working in M&E. It covers configuring DHIS2 datasets and dashboards, assessing data quality, designing indicators, and presenting findings to decision-makers.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for mid-career professionals who work directly with health programme data — whether collecting it, managing it, analysing it, or reporting it to national authorities and international funders. You should have at least one year of practical experience working with a health information system or M&E function before attending.
modules: Health Programme M&E in the Digital Age
DHIS2 Analytics, Dashboards, and Data Visualisation
Mobile Data Collection for Community Health Programmes
Data Quality Assessment in Health Programmes
Programme Performance Reporting and Stakeholder Communication
prerequisites: Participants should bring a laptop with a modern web browser (Chrome or Firefox recommended) and reliable internet access for DHIS2 training instance exercises. No software installation is required — all DHIS2 and KoboToolbox exercises run in-browser. Pre-loaded training datasets and exercise templates will be provided by the facilitator. A basic working knowledge of health programme indicator concepts and at least one year of experience in an M&E, health information, or programme management role is expected before attending.
